body: This interface is too broad. It violates the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) by forcing all implementers to support print, scan, and fax, even if they only need one of these capabilities.

Throwing UnsupportedOperationException for methods mandated by the interface is a clear sign that the interface is too "fat". The client should not be forced to depend on methods that are not implemented.
Same as above. This is a violation of ISP.
Same as Java: This abstract base class is too monolithic. Consider splitting it into smaller, more specific interfaces (e.g., IPrinter, IScanner, IFax).
Raising NotImplementedError here indicates a violation of ISP. This class is forced to implement methods it doesn't need.
Same as above. This is a violation of ISP.
